meta.description: Source-available vehicle diagnostics, battery health and live telemetry for supported Volvo and Polestar vehicles over DoIP and UDS. Local, private and for personal use.

home.title: Hanterill | Vehicle Diagnostics for Volvo & Polestar
home.desc: Source-available vehicle diagnostics, battery health and live telemetry for supported Volvo and Polestar vehicles over DoIP and UDS. Local, private and for personal use.

features.title: Features
features.desc: Battery health, full vehicle diagnostics, live telemetry, subsystem telemetry, scored inspection reports, session evidence and gated service functions, all over one direct DoIP connection.

batteryHealth.title: Battery health
batteryHealth.desc: Read state of health and charge, pack voltage, per-cell-group potentials, imbalance and thermal data reported by the vehicle battery management system.

vehicleDiagnostics.title: Vehicle diagnostics
vehicleDiagnostics.desc: ECU discovery over DoIP, identification data, DTCs by status with freeze frames, all-module DID scans, firmware inventory and gated clearing.

liveData.title: Live data
liveData.desc: Live engineering telemetry: pack voltage and current, battery and inverter temperature, motor torque and 12 V system voltage, with on-demand periodic sampling.

systemTelemetry.title: System telemetry
systemTelemetry.desc: Subsystem read views beyond the battery: climate loop, drive units, charging and power, TCAM, steering, service schedule, GPS and the vehicle option map.

inspectionReports.title: Inspection reports
inspectionReports.desc: A scored pre-purchase inspection built from read-only diagnostics: pack degradation, cell balance, fault severity and odometer consistency, each verdict traceable to a versioned rule.

sessionsEvidence.title: Sessions and evidence
sessionsEvidence.desc: Diagnostic sessions archive locally and compare inside the app: fault code diffs, cell-by-cell pack history, firmware before and after, operator notes and exports.

serviceFunctions.title: Service functions
serviceFunctions.desc: EPB service mode, 12 V battery adaptation, service reminder reset, damper calibration and DTC clearing: implemented, compiled out of released builds and gated behind an explicit unsafe-write feature.

vehicles.title: Supported vehicles
vehicles.desc: Hanterill is CMA-first: Polestar 2 and the CMA Volvos are the tested platforms. SPA and SEA1 battery catalogues ship pending hardware verification; SPA2 and Zeekr remain research.

download.title: Download
download.desc: Download Hanterill for Windows, macOS or Linux. Release details come from GitHub Releases.

about.pIndependence: Hanterill is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, maintained by, sponsored by or authorised by Volvo Cars, Polestar or Geely. Manufacturer and model names are used only to describe which vehicles the software can communicate with. No manufacturer logo is used as a mark of endorsement.
about.pLicense: The source is available to read. Hanterill is provided for personal, non-commercial use under the project license, and is not open source in the OSI sense. The <link>license page</link> has the terms.
about.pWhy: The diagnostic data a modern EV holds about its own battery and drivetrain is detailed and useful, and most of it is readable with standard protocols. Hanterill makes that data available to owners without a proprietary interface or a recurring fee.
about.pHow: The diagnostic engine, DoIP stack and decoders are Rust. The desktop shell is Tauri v2, so there is no bundled browser engine. The interface is React and TypeScript, typed against the engine.
about.pContrib: The most useful contributions are protocol traces, ECU maps and decoder corrections. The repository has the details.

download.pSource: The repository is public and the source is readable, for private and non-commercial use under the project license. Packaged downloads come from the release page. Building from source is not a supported installation path yet.
download.pVerify: Releases are tagged in the repository and publish checksums alongside the binaries. Match the checksum of your download against the one listed on the release page before running it.
download.pCadence: Versions follow SemVer tags. The panel shows the latest published release and its assets; if GitHub cannot be reached it links to the releases page.

stays: Every diagnostic session, DTC read and live capture
never: No crash reporting to a third party
privacy.pVin: The VIN is read as part of vehicle identification. In logs and exports, Hanterill redacts it where it is not required, so a shared session file does not carry a full VIN by default. Per-vehicle caches are keyed by a hash of the VIN.
privacy.pNetwork: During a session, Hanterill communicates only with the vehicle over the local Ethernet link. The website may query the GitHub API to show the latest release; the application itself does not require any internet connection to run.
privacy.pNoSub: There is no paid tier and no license server. The source is available to read and there is nothing to monetise in your vehicle data.

safety.pReadOnly: Battery data, ECU identification, fault codes and live telemetry are all read operations. Running them cannot change vehicle configuration. Released builds transmit read services only: what the binary can do is reported by a capability manifest.
safety.pChanges: Clearing diagnostic information, service routines and adaptations alter ECU state. They are not in released builds: they compile only with an explicit unsafe-write feature, and the interface hides every command the binary cannot execute. There is no setting that turns a released build into a write-capable one.
safety.pHv: Electric vehicles carry hazardous high-voltage systems. Reading battery data over a diagnostic link does not de-energise anything and does not make physical high-voltage service safe. HV service requires procedures, equipment and training from the manufacturer.
safety.hNoSubstitute: Not a substitute for manufacturer tooling
safety.pNoSubstitute: Hanterill is an independent project. It does not replace the diagnostic system supplied by the manufacturer, and it is not affiliated with Volvo Cars, Polestar or Geely. Use it to understand your vehicle, not as the sole basis for a safety-critical repair decision.
safety.pUnverified: On Testing or Research platforms, decoding is not verified. Do not rely on battery figures or fault interpretation, and do not make purchase or repair decisions from them.

batteryHealth.pWhere: State of health is reported by the battery management system, not calculated by Hanterill. Hanterill reads it, and the values behind it, directly from the vehicle.
reads: State of health and state of charge
Every cell-group potential on the pack topology in force (108 on CMA: 27 modules, 4 groups each)
Minimum, maximum and delta across cell groups
Pack and module temperatures, rendered as a thermal grid
Cross-signal checks: reported pack voltage against the cell sum, reported power against calculated
batteryHealth.pTopologies: The cell matrix is not hard-coded. The catalogue models CMA 108S, the SPA EV 96S and 108S packs, the SPA hybrid 102-cell T8 pack and the SEA 107S and 110S variants, and a 102-cell pack reports complete at 102. Only the CMA topology is verified on a live vehicle; the others are catalogued and awaiting hardware confirmation.
batteryHealth.pEngineering: Switch the panel to Engineering for the control module, transport, service and identifiers. Battery diagnostics docs have the full read sequence.
batteryHealth.moreSoh: How state of health is read

vehicleDiagnostics.pDiscovery: A UDP identification request on port 13400 enumerates responders. Hanterill then opens a TCP channel, activates routing, and probes each address for a UDS session. A functional broadcast can query every ECU at once, falling back to individual probes only for the ones that stay quiet. The CMA catalogue holds 43 modules; 34 advertise DTC support. Discovery is fast because absent modules are remembered per vehicle, keyed by a hash of the VIN, never by the VIN itself.
vehicleDiagnostics.pFaults: DTCs are read with the ReadDTCInformation service and reported with their status: active, pending, stored or historical. The list opens on the codes that need attention. Where the ECU kept a freeze frame or snapshot, Hanterill retrieves it alongside the code, and a built-in diff compares any two scans.
vehicleDiagnostics.pClearing: Clearing (UDS 0x14) mirrors the reference tool's orchestration: per-ECU progress, freeze-frame capture before the erase, a verify re-read that reports the stubborn set, and optional link recovery after a module reboot. It is not compiled into released builds: it exists only behind the explicit unsafe-write feature, and the running binary reports its real capabilities through a manifest.
vehicleDiagnostics.pDid: A bounded scan sweeps known data identifiers across the whole catalogue in one pass, recording per-row negative response codes, digests and latency. The DID Explorer replays stored captures offline, so a CSV from one session can be mined without a vehicle attached.
vehicleDiagnostics.pInventory: VIN, ECU part numbers, hardware and software versions and supplier identifiers are read with ReadDataByIdentifier, producing a hardware and software inventory of the car. Two inventories diff ECU by ECU, for example before and after an OTA. Multi-ECU odometer reads cross-check each other and flag disagreement.
vehicleDiagnostics.pEvidence: A session exports to JSON or CSV and archives locally. Run one before a repair and one after: the built-in comparison shows fewer codes and fewer active faults. <link>Sessions and evidence</link> covers the comparison views.

liveData.pChannels: Toggle channels above the chart. Any readable data identifier can be added to a live view; common drivetrain and battery channels are grouped by default. Where the ECU supports it, sampling uses the UDS periodic read (0x2A): one on-demand registration, then the module streams. Sampling rate is bounded by the ECU and the diagnostic session, not by Hanterill.
liveData.pReading: Hover for a synchronised crosshair. Tap or press Live to pause and inspect a point. The stream keeps one guard: a single live stream at a time, cancellable per operation, with dropped intervals counted and shown rather than smoothed away. The trace here is a deterministic simulated drive cycle, not a vehicle reading.
liveData.pExport: A running view can be written to CSV for offline analysis.

serviceFunctions.warningLead: Released builds cannot do any of this.
serviceFunctions.warningBody: The operations below are compiled out unless the software is deliberately built with the unsafe-write feature. The running binary publishes a capability manifest, and the interface hides every command the binary cannot execute. There is no toggle that turns a released build into a write-capable one.
routines: Car-wide or per-module clear, with verify re-read
serviceFunctions.pClearing: Where it is compiled in, the clear path matches the reverse-engineered reference orchestration: enter the extended session per module, capture freeze frames before the erase (the clear wipes them), bulk clear, wait through the pending window, retry the laggards per ECU, then re-read and report the stubborn set. An optional force-reset loop reboots stubborn modules and repairs the DoIP routing afterwards. It is suppressed while the vehicle reports a driving usage mode. Pre-erase and post-clear states feed the built-in <link>DTC diff</link>.
serviceFunctions.pAvail: Routine support depends on the ECU and the platform. A routine that is not implemented for a given vehicle is not shown. Testing and Research platforms do not expose service functions at all, and the routine identifiers themselves are pending a per-operation safety design review even in write-capable builds.

domains: A single grade composed from the domains below.
State of health read from the BMS, graded against documented bands.
Spread across cell groups on the topology in force.
Faults weighted by status and class, not counted flat.
Mileage cross-read across modules; disagreement is its own finding.
inspectionReports.pRules: The score is produced by a deterministic, versioned rule engine. Every rule cites the class of evidence it rests on, and the class caps the strongest verdict the rule may force. A published standard can flag attention. A community heuristic can only add a note. Provisional decoders downgrade their rules automatically.
inspectionReports.pMissing: An unanswered channel is recorded as missing and the grade degrades toward inconclusive. Missing data never passes silently and never fails loudly: it is shown as what it is. The same engine carries advisory-only rules, such as coolant temperature spread, overdue service intervals and DC-DC bus voltage, which annotate the report without moving the score.
inspectionReports.pReport: The report page assembles identity, battery, fault, ECU, service and thermal findings into one printable document with a checksum, partial-coverage tolerance and an explanation of the rubric. Historical sessions can be re-scored under current rules without touching the car again. GPS position is removed from inspection reports, and remaining coordinates are rounded to roughly 110 metres.
inspectionReports.pBuying: One session over the cable covers what a pre-purchase inspection needs here: true state of health from the BMS, cell balance, full-vehicle fault history with freeze frames, service counters and tamper cross-checks. <link>The rule design is documented</link> so any number in the report can be argued with.

pages: Heat pump loop, compressor state, coolant temperatures per loop with the deltas computed, condenser against evaporator.
Front and rear inverter telemetry (IHFA, IEM) with a side-by-side comparison: temperature, voltage, coolant, torque split. A side that did not answer stays empty, never zero.
Socket lock, cable capability, on-board charger state, plus a charge-limitation diagnosis that attributes a capped charge from evidence or declines to.
Charger AC input and DC-DC converter, with the 12 V rail tracked against its state of charge.
Emergency backup-battery health with a length-discriminated layout, raw byte evidence and a digest; GNSS fix only on an explicit button press.
Steering angle sensor: angle, angular velocity, calibration state. Read-only; zeroing is not part of it.
DIM intervals with mileage and time countdowns, and a flag when a counter moves somewhere it should not.
The CEM 256-entry option map with live search, plus the factory build record: anchor VIN, option codes, paint and interior trim.
12 V quiescent current history and module wake-state logs for parasitic-drain chasing.
systemTelemetry.pMeasured: Each field on these pages is a typed observation: value, state, source and decoder version, or an honest failure. A DID that refuses with a negative response code produces a refusal, not a zero. A parked car with a drifting rotor reading is classified stationary at the display layer without touching the raw value.
systemTelemetry.pChecks: Ten cross-signal checks compare the story the vehicle tells against itself: pack voltage against the sum of its cells, reported power against calculated, current plausibility while parked, compressor state against refrigerant pressure, axle coolant deltas. They run on the live battery, motor and climate reads. A check that is missing an input records it as insufficient data. None of them claims a fault: the worst verdict is a warning.
systemTelemetry.pBoundaries: Cable-rating decoding stays experimental. Option indexes the catalogue does not name remain numeric. Unknown layouts are kept as exploratory evidence rather than turned into a verdict about your car.

diffs: Two scans of the same car: codes added, codes cleared, status changes, snapshot evidence kept.
Two cell lists matched by physical index. A cell populated on only one side keeps a gap, never a zero.
Two inventories compared ECU by ECU: unchanged, software changed, hardware changed, new, missing, unknown.
A stored session re-graded under the current rule version.
sessionsEvidence.pArchive: Every session is written to a durable local store: atomic saves, corrupt-file recovery, a cross-restart history and your own operator notes per session. Nothing leaves the machine. The store is also where the per-vehicle profile cache lives, keyed by a hash of the VIN so a directory listing never exposes an identity.
sessionsEvidence.pCompare: The comparison views take any two stored sessions and show them side by side across DTC, battery, ECU and firmware domains. The point is evidence you can point at: fewer active codes after the repair, a stable cell spread after balancing, the exact firmware delta an OTA left behind.
sessionsEvidence.pReplay: Captures are data. A stored DID scan CSV can be replayed and analysed without a vehicle attached, and the support bundle export scrubs serial numbers, private addresses, credentials and coordinates before a file ever leaves the machine.
sessionsEvidence.pExports: Sessions and reports export to versioned JSON and CSV (formula-injection neutralised) or a ZIP bundle. The report page prints through the browser with styled print CSS, so the paper copy matches the screen. VIN is redacted in exports by default.
sessionsEvidence.cliLink: Script the same output from the CLI
sessionsEvidence.pUsesArchive: The inspection report uses the same archive: <link>scored condition grades</link> re-computable from stored evidence at any time.

features.title: Everything the vehicle will tell you, over one connection.

features.batteryBody: State of health and charge, pack voltage, cell-group spread, min, max and delta, and pack temperature. Cross-checks compare reported figures against the measured cells and flag disagreements. The percentage your dashboard shows, and the numbers behind it.
features.scanBody: Hanterill discovers ECUs over DoIP, identifies which speak UDS, and reads the identification, hardware and software data from each. 43 modules in the CMA catalogue, 34 of them DTC-capable, probed in one pass.
features.faultBody: Hanterill reads DTCs with their status: active now, pending, stored or historical. The list opens on the codes that need attention. If the ECU saved a snapshot when the fault set, you get that too, with a built-in diff between scans.
features.liveBody: Pack voltage and current, battery and inverter temperature, motor torque, the 12 V system. Sampled with on-demand periodic reads and plotted on fixed axes.

blurbs.CMA: Compact Modular Architecture. The tested platform: Polestar 2 and the smaller electric Volvos. 108 cell groups, 27 modules by 4.
blurbs.SPA: Scalable Product Architecture. First-generation Recharge cars. The hybrid and EV pack topologies, the CAN-era BECM map and the decoders ship in the catalogue, pending live-vehicle verification.
blurbs.SEA: Sustainable Experience Architecture. The SEA1 registry, DoIP routing addresses, DID catalogue and cell mapping for EX30-class cars are defined. Hardware confirmation is pending.
blurbs.SPA2: Second-generation SPA. Different gateway and security model. Under investigation.

protocolStack.title: Built on automotive standards.
protocolStack.lead: Hanterill talks to the car's diagnostic network with the same protocols a dealer tool uses. Nothing in between is a proprietary cloud service.
protocolStack.paragraph: A session starts with UDP discovery on port 13400, opens a TCP channel and activates routing. Discovery can also address all ECUs at once with a functional broadcast. Reads then run as UDS: session control, read by identifier, read DTC information, on-demand periodic sampling and routine results. Released builds transmit read services only.

safety.title: Read-only by default. Writes are compiled out.
safety.lead: Released builds of Hanterill transmit read services only. The operations that change the vehicle are not in them: they exist only in builds made with an explicit unsafe-write feature, and the app reports its real boundaries through a capability manifest.
safety.highVoltageBody: Electric vehicles carry hazardous high-voltage systems. Reading data over a cable does not make it safe to work on them, and Hanterill is not a substitute for the manufacturer's service procedures.

home.q: Do I need a special diagnostic tool or dongle?
home.a: No. A passive ENET cable (OBD-II to RJ45) and any Ethernet interface on your computer are enough for DoIP on supported vehicles. None of the usual OBD dongles are involved.

home.q: Does Hanterill send any data anywhere?
home.a: No. It communicates only with the vehicle and writes results to your disk. There is no account, no backend, no analytics and no telemetry. The VIN is kept out of logs and exports unless something needs it.

Polestar 2 and the CMA-platform Volvos (XC40/EX40, C40/EC40) are the tested platforms. SPA and SEA1 (EX30, Polestar 4) have battery catalogues, decoders and pack topologies shipping in the app, but nothing on those cars is hardware-verified yet, so they are labelled Testing. Zeekr, Lynk & Co and SPA2 remain research.

Released builds transmit read-only services. Clearing, routines and writes are not compiled into them: they exist only in builds made with an explicit unsafe-write feature for authorized service work. High-voltage service still requires the manufacturer's procedures.

home.q: Is this an official Volvo or Polestar tool?
home.a: No. Hanterill is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, maintained by or authorised by Volvo Cars, Polestar or Geely. The source is available to read. It is provided for personal, non-commercial use.

home.q: What can I do with the battery data?
home.a: Read state of health and charge, pack voltage, per-cell-group potentials for every populated position (108 on CMA, plus SPA and SEA pack topologies), min/max/delta and pack temperature, and export a session to compare before and after a repair.

home.q: Can I use it without a car?
home.a: Yes. The connection page carries deterministic simulation vehicles (healthy baseline, fault-injected and sleep-drain scenarios), so every screen can be exercised offline. Simulated sessions are always labelled as simulated.

home.q: What does the inspection report give me?
home.a: A scored vehicle-condition grade built from the same reads: pack degradation, cell balance, fault severity and odometer consistency, each traceable to a documented rule version. Historical sessions can be re-scored when the rules are updated. GPS position never appears in reports.

compat.q: Does Hanterill work with any Volvo or Polestar?
compat.a: No. Hanterill is CMA-first. Polestar 2 and the CMA Volvos (XC40/EX40, C40/EC40) are the tested platforms. SPA and SEA1 have shipped battery catalogues and decoders pending hardware verification, and are labelled Testing. Zeekr, Lynk & Co and SPA2 are Research.

compat.q: What is the difference between platform compatibility and support?
compat.a: Platform compatibility means Hanterill can reach the vehicle over DoIP. Support means the diagnostic functions are implemented and verified against known-good references. Being reachable does not make the data trustworthy, which is why Testing and Research platforms are labelled separately.

compat.q: My car is listed as Testing or Research. Can I use it?
compat.a: You can connect and, on some, read identification data. Do not rely on battery figures or fault interpretation, and do not run service routines. Testing and Research mean the decoding is not verified on a live vehicle.

compat.q: Is this endorsed by Volvo or Polestar?
compat.a: No. Hanterill is an independent project, not affiliated with, maintained by or authorised by Volvo Cars, Polestar or Geely. Manufacturer names are used only to describe compatibility.

footer.blurb: Full diagnostics for Volvo and Polestar, running on your own computer.
footer.disclaimer: Hanterill is an independent project, not affiliated with, maintained by, sponsored by or authorised by Volvo Cars, Polestar or Geely. Manufacturer names are used only to describe compatibility. Source-available, private use only.
footer.tagline: For owners who want control over their car.

pages.featuresLead: The whole coverage, read over the same connection. Standard diagnostics stay read-only; write-capable functions are separated and not part of released builds.
pages.batteryHealthTitle: The percentage, and the numbers behind it.
pages.batteryHealthLead: Hanterill reads high-voltage battery data reported by the vehicle: state of health and charge, pack voltage, cell-group distribution, imbalance and temperature, across every pack topology the catalogue knows.
pages.vehicleDiagnosticsTitle: Every ECU on the network, not just the one with the light on.
pages.vehicleDiagnosticsLead: Hanterill discovers the vehicle ECUs over DoIP, identifies which speak UDS, and reads fault, identification and data-identifier content from each.
pages.liveDataTitle: Engineering telemetry on a polling loop.
pages.liveDataLead: Hanterill polls and subscribes to data identifiers and plots them like instrumentation software: fixed axes, thin traces, no decoration.
pages.serviceFunctionsTitle: The operations that change the vehicle stay separate.
pages.serviceFunctionsLead: Where the platform supports them, Hanterill can run service routines and adaptations. They are compiled out of released builds and gated behind an explicit unsafe-write feature.
pages.inspectionReportsTitle: Before you buy it: a score you can defend.
pages.inspectionReportsLead: Hanterill turns the same reads into a graded pre-purchase inspection, with every verdict traceable to a documented rule.
pages.sessionsEvidenceTitle: The history of the car, kept on your machine.
pages.sessionsEvidenceLead: Sessions archive locally and compare inside the app: fault codes, cell potentials, firmware, before and after.
pages.systemTelemetryLead: Each subsystem with a read path gets its own page: climate, drive units, charging, power, TCAM, steering, service schedule, GPS and the vehicle option map.
pages.vehiclesTitle: CMA tested, SPA and SEA1 catalogued.
pages.vehiclesLead: Select a platform and a vehicle to see exactly which functions are verified. Each status label reflects what has been checked on that car, not just the platform it is built on.
pages.downloadLead: Native builds for each desktop platform. Nothing installs automatically and nothing phones home.
pages.changelogLead: Each tagged build with its notes, newest first, read from GitHub Releases. Versions follow SemVer; the full change history is kept per version.
pages.safetyTitle: What is safe, and what is not.
pages.safetyLead: Diagnostic software can read a great deal and change a few things. Hanterill is built so you always know which is which.
pages.privacyLead: Hanterill has no backend and no account system. It talks to the vehicle and writes to your disk. That is the whole data path.
pages.aboutTitle: A project for people who want to understand their vehicles.
pages.aboutLead: Hanterill started as a way to read CMA battery data without a dealer subscription. It grew into a general DoIP and UDS diagnostic tool.
pages.screenshotsTitle: The app on a real car.
pages.screenshotsLead: Hanterill running on a supported Volvo and Polestar: overview, battery, fault codes, live data, subsystem pages and the scored inspection report.
pages.projectsTitle: More tools from the same bench.
pages.projectsLead: Hanterill is not the only project here. These are other independent tools from the same author, built with the same local-first approach.
pages.projectsSeparate: Each project is maintained separately, with its own repository, license and release schedule.
pages.networkLead: Every control unit on the CMA platform as an interactive wiring map: 170 units, 295 typed links across nine networks and 622 documented pin rows. Filter by bus, trace a path between any two modules, and read the connector pin-outs the diagnostics run on.

network.disclaimer: Independent enthusiast documentation of the CMA electrical architecture. Not affiliated with or endorsed by any vehicle manufacturer.
